hed: A Quiet Morning on the Desk
deck: Table Rock this morning: 909.60 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Midge. Down. Slow.
play.body: Winter rainbows eat tiny and they eat on the pause. If you can't see your fly, you're fishing.

season.name: Winter trout
season.why: Table Rock gets quiet and vertical. Taneycomo becomes the reason you came. This is Johnny Morris water — cold, clear, and honest.
tips: Spoon or ice jig over 30–50 feet on Table Rock if you must. Most people shouldn't.
Taneycomo is the trip: midges, eggs, pink worms, tiny jigs, 2-pound test.
Generation still rules. A winter blowdown is a drift day.
Felt soles and a staff if you wad. The rocks don't care that you're on vacation.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: The pool walked down from 910.09 early in the week to 909.60 this morning — about 0.49 ft off that earlier mark, still under the 915 full pool. 2 mornings this week the desk had no new gage (carry-forward). Numbers marked “desk” were read from that day’s scout; “carry” was not. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — scout does not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: At roughly 909.6 ft the lake shows significantly more exposed shoreline than in summer. Stumps, hazards, and shallow areas in coves and creek arms (especially James, Kings, and Long Creek) sit closer to the surface — navigate slowly and plan for longer walks at some launches.

Surface water has cooled into the upper 50s with gin-clear visibility. Bass hit topwaters and soft plastics in low light before transitioning to jigs, drop-shot, tubes, or live bait around long points, gravel flats dropping into deeper water, and offshore structure. Walleye and crappie continue producing around brush piles and points. In these clear, cooling conditions precise natural presentations outperform flashy or sloppy rigs as fish feed heavily ahead of winter.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad. Do not guess the generators.

body: This cold tailwater, fed by deep releases from Table Rock, stays productive year-round thanks to consistent MDC stocking. Generation dictates tactics: low or minimum flows open wading, light-line drifting, or indicator fishing in seams and soft water; stronger pulses require added weight, drifting current breaks, and heavier line (2–4 lb test).

From Table Rock Dam down to Fall Creek is trophy water — artificial lures and flies only; no soft plastics, scented, or natural baits permitted. Rainbows 12–20 inches must be released. Save pink worms, PowerBait, or scented/scented baits for water below Fall Creek. A trout permit is required in many stretches. Recent reports note solid rainbow numbers with increasing brown trout in the upper lake on marabou jigs (black, sculpin, olive), zebra midges, scuds, small streamers, and eggs. Clarity is generally excellent. Always call 866-494-1993 for the latest SWPA generation schedule before you go and stay well outside the closed zone below the dam.

editor.note: Two-lake daily rebuilt from the morning fishing scout plus the prior week of files. We print a level only when the scout had one. Carry-forward mornings are labeled. No invented bite ratings. Call 866-494-1993 before wading Taneycomo.
